questions.stem: A plant has the genotype Tt for height, where T (tall) is dominant over t (short). What is the phenotype of this plant, and is it homozygous or heterozygous?

options.text: Short and homozygous
Tall and homozygous
Short and heterozygous
Tall and heterozygous

questions.explanation: The genotype Tt has two different alleles (one dominant T, one recessive t), making it heterozygous. Since T is dominant, only one copy is needed to express the tall phenotype. The recessive allele t is present but masked by the dominant allele. The plant appears tall despite carrying the short allele.

questions.stem: Two organisms have the same phenotype for a trait but different genotypes. Which pair of genotypes could produce the same phenotype if the trait shows simple dominance?

options.text: BB and Bb
BB and bb
Bb and bb
BB and Bb would always look different

questions.explanation: In simple dominance, BB (homozygous dominant) and Bb (heterozygous) both express the dominant phenotype because at least one dominant allele is present. They look the same despite having different genotypes. Only bb (homozygous recessive) shows the recessive phenotype. This is why you cannot always determine genotype from phenotype alone.

questions.stem: A breeder wants to determine whether a black-furred rabbit (where black B is dominant over white b) is homozygous (BB) or heterozygous (Bb). What cross should they perform?

options.text: Cross it with another black rabbit
Cross it with a white rabbit (bb) - if any white offspring appear, the parent must be Bb
Examine the rabbit's parents to see if they are black or white
It is impossible to determine the genotype

questions.explanation: This is called a test cross. By crossing the unknown black rabbit with a homozygous recessive white rabbit (bb), the offspring reveal the parent's genotype. If the parent is BB, all offspring will be Bb (black). If the parent is Bb, approximately half the offspring will be Bb (black) and half will be bb (white). Any white offspring prove the parent is heterozygous.

questions.stem: In genetics, the term 'allele' is sometimes confused with 'gene'. Which statement correctly distinguishes between a gene and an allele?

options.text: A gene is found on a chromosome; an allele is found in the cytoplasm
A gene and an allele mean exactly the same thing
A gene is a section of DNA coding for a protein; alleles are different versions of that gene
An allele is a section of DNA; a gene is the protein it produces

questions.explanation: A gene is a length of DNA that codes for a particular protein (e.g., the gene for eye colour). Alleles are different forms of the same gene caused by differences in the DNA base sequence (e.g., the allele for blue eyes vs. the allele for brown eyes). Each person inherits two alleles for each gene - one from each parent.

questions.stem: A student writes: 'An organism with genotype Bb has a 50% chance of passing on the dominant allele to each offspring.' Is this correct?

options.text: No, it has a 100% chance because the dominant allele is always passed on
No, it has a 75% chance because dominant alleles are more likely to be inherited
Yes, during meiosis alleles separate so each gamete has an equal chance of receiving either the B or b allele
No, it depends on whether the other parent is homozygous or heterozygous

questions.explanation: The student is correct. During meiosis, the two alleles in a heterozygous (Bb) organism separate into different gametes. Each gamete receives one allele, so there is a 50% chance of receiving B and a 50% chance of receiving b. This is Mendel's law of segregation. The probability applies regardless of whether the allele is dominant or recessive.
